dna.title: Wrong instrument DNA
dna.body: Gold moves 100-300 points a day. NAS100 moves 500-800. Trailing stops tuned for XAUUSD hemorrhage profit the moment you point them at an index.

hedge.title: Wrong hedge logic
hedge.body: Symmetric hedging assumes a range-bound market. NAS100 and US30 have carried an upward bias for decades — a BUY-heavy strategy captures more of that, not less.

timing.title: Wrong entry scale
timing.body: EMA-based entries that work on gold at $2,000 do not translate to an index at $20,000. The timing has to be recalibrated to the scale of the price.

solution.title: Built for indices from the first line

native.title: Index-native strategy
native.body: Not a gold EA repurposed. Every parameter — entry timing, hedge triggers, trail distances, exit targets — was tuned specifically for NAS100 and US30 volatility patterns.

trail.title: Fast Points Trail (v1.1)
trail.body: EMA-based trailing lags by hundreds of points on fast indices. Topstock's Fast Points Trail reacts within 300 points of price — protecting profit before the giveback.

howItWorks.title: Four stages of the mechanism
howItWorks.description: Every figure below is the real value from the EA source, not a marketing number.

entry.title: Anticipation Batch Entry
entry.body: When price enters the last 20% of the EMA100→EMA200 gap, Topstock opens a 5-order batch anticipating the reversal. Direction is set by EMA100 against EMA200.

confirm.title: Cross Confirmation
confirm.body: If price crosses EMA100 in the batch direction, one additional confirmation order is added — increasing size in the direction of momentum.

recovery.title: Independent Grid Recovery
recovery.body: All 6 grids operate independently. The first hedge level triggers at 1,500 points adverse (ANT batch) or 1,000 points (Cross order), and every level after that steps every 1,000 points. Every hedge is a BUY.

exit.title: Dynamic Exit
exit.body: A grid closes when net P/L reaches a target scaled to position size: 300 points × total lots × value per point. The bigger the grid, the proportionally bigger the move it needs.

items.selfHealing: Self-healing close logic retries automatically when the broker rejects an order
items.iterationCap: Hard cap of 30 iterations per tick prevents runaway loops
items.phaseManagement: V2 phase management preserves the original position throughout recovery

nature.title: The nature of index CFD risk
nature.body:
The NASDAQ 100 and US 30 are highly volatile instruments, moving 500-800 points in an ordinary day and far more around major economic releases or unexpected events.

Trading with leverage magnifies both gains and losses. You can lose the entire balance of your account in a short period.

grid.title: Risks specific to grid strategies
grid.body:
Topstock averages into positions using a grid, opening further positions as price moves against it.

This carries characteristics you need to understand: floating loss deepens with the distance price travels against you, and if price runs against the position further than your capital can support, it can lead to a margin call or a forced stop out, realising a substantial loss.

Capping hedge levels with the InpRecMaxLevel parameter helps control this, but does not remove it.

automation.title: Risks from automation
automation.body:
An automated system depends on technical factors the software cannot control: your internet connection, the stability of your VPS or computer, your broker's server availability, execution latency, requotes, and slippage.

Any of these can cause the system to behave differently from its design, and to affect your results.

Backtests are calculated from historical data under simulated conditions, which cannot fully reproduce live trading.

Things a backtest commonly fails to reflect include real slippage during volatile periods, spread widening around news, broker order rejections, and connection latency.

Past performance neither indicates nor guarantees future performance in any circumstance.

howItWorks.title: How Topstock EA works
howItWorks.summary: Every stage explained — entry, recovery, trailing, and exit — with the real parameter values taken from the EA source.
howItWorks.sourceNote: Every figure on this page is copied straight from the EA source, not written for marketing. If you want to verify any of it before buying, ask us on LINE.

entry.title: Anticipation Batch Entry
entry.body:
Topstock reads direction from the EMA 20/50/100/200 structure of the AURUM PRO system.

When price moves into the last 20% of the gap between EMA100 and EMA200, the system treats that as a zone with a high chance of reversal and opens a batch of 5 orders to anticipate it.

The batch direction is set by how EMA100 sits against EMA200 — not by an oscillator or a chart pattern.

confirmation.title: Cross Confirmation
confirmation.body:
Once the anticipation batch is open, if price crosses EMA100 in the same direction as the batch, the system treats momentum as confirming the direction and adds one further order.

This Cross order carries different recovery terms from the ANT batch: its first hedge level sits at 1,000 points rather than 1,500. It entered on confirmation, so a shorter adverse move is expected.

recovery.title: Independent Grid Recovery
recovery.body:
Topstock runs 6 grids that are completely independent of one another. One grid entering recovery does not drag the others with it — each keeps its own hedge levels, profit target, and state.

The first hedge level triggers at 1,500 points adverse for the ANT batch, or 1,000 points for the Cross order. Every level after that steps every 1,000 points.

The important part: every hedge is a BUY. This is not symmetric hedging that opens against the position — it averages into the direction in which US indices have carried a long-term upward bias.

You cap the number of levels with the InpRecMaxLevel parameter; we recommend 8-10.

trailing.title: Fast Points Trail (new in v1.1)
trailing.body:
This is what v1.1 added, and the main reason Topstock handles indices better than a general-purpose EA.

Trailing that relies on EMAs alone cannot keep up with an index moving 500-800 points a day. By the time the EMA has caught up, several hundred points of profit have already gone back to the market.

Fast Points Trail arms once profit reaches +500 points, then trails the stop 300 points behind current price — tight, and quick to react.

It runs alongside the original EMA-based trail rather than replacing it: whichever produces the tighter stop is the one that applies.

exit.title: Dynamic Exit
exit.body:
A grid closes as a whole when its net P/L reaches a target calculated dynamically: 300 points × the grid's total lots × the value per point.

Why the target has to scale: if a grid grows from 0.05 to 0.40 lots during recovery, a fixed target would close it far too early to justify the risk it carried. This formula makes a bigger grid require a proportionally bigger move.

And because the target is measured on the whole grid's net P/L, the system never closes the winning orders and leaves the losing ones open.

selfHealing.title: Self-healing close
selfHealing.body: When the broker rejects a close (requote, off quotes, market closed), the system retries automatically until it succeeds rather than leaving an order in a state nobody intended.

noLockLoss.title: Never locks in losses
noLockLoss.body: The system does not automatically close a grid that is still net negative in order to "cut the loss". Closing happens on reaching the profit target only. Deciding to close at a loss is your call, not the EA's.

iterationCap.title: 30 iterations per tick
iterationCap.body: Every piece of logic is capped at 30 iterations per tick as a hard ceiling, so neither a bug nor an abnormal market condition can leave the EA opening orders without end.

phaseManagement.title: V2 phase management
phaseManagement.body: Each grid's state is tracked as a distinct phase, which keeps the original position intact through recovery instead of letting it disappear among the hedges added on top.

hedging.title: The account must be Hedging, not Netting
hedging.body: Topstock holds several positions on the same symbol at once. A netting account merges them into a single position, which stops the grid system working at all. This is the most important item on the list, and it cannot be changed later.

spread.title: Average spread on the index
spread.body: Ask for the average NAS100 spread while the US session is open. A spread that is too wide eats meaningfully into the 300-point target behind every close.

stopLevel.title: Stop level and freeze level
stopLevel.body: Some brokers enforce a minimum distance between current price and the stop loss. If that distance exceeds 300 points, Fast Points Trail cannot work as designed.

contractSize.title: Contract size and value per point
contractSize.body: Check what one lot of NAS100 is worth per point. That value feeds directly into the close-target formula, and it varies a lot between brokers.

sessions.title: Trading hours and breaks
sessions.body: Indices have intraday breaks and close over the weekend. Check the broker's server time against your own so you know when the EA is actually active.

cta.title: Not sure your broker will work?
cta.description: Send us the broker and account type and we'll tell you whether it runs, and what to configure.

setup.title: Installing Topstock EA
setup.summary: An overview of the five installation steps. The full guide, with screenshots and preset files, is delivered after purchase.

download.title: Download the EA file
download.body:
After payment you receive Topstock EA v1.1 (.ex5) along with preset files for NAS100 and US30, sent over LINE or by email.

The .ex5 file is already compiled — there is nothing to build yourself.

install.title: Copy the file into your MT5 folder
install.body:
In MetaTrader 5, open File → Open Data Folder, then go into MQL5 → Experts and drop the .ex5 file there.

Put the preset files into MQL5 → Presets.

enable.title: Restart MT5 and enable Algo Trading
enable.body:
Close and reopen MetaTrader 5. The EA appears in the Navigator panel under Expert Advisors.

Switch the Algo Trading button on the toolbar to green. With it off, the EA sends no orders at all, however correctly it is installed.

attach.title: Drag the EA onto a chart
attach.body:
Open an M5 chart for NAS100 (or whatever your broker calls it) and drag Topstock EA from the Navigator onto it.

In the dialog, tick Allow Algo Trading on the Common tab, then open the Inputs tab to load the preset we sent you.

verify.title: Confirm it's running
verify.body:
When installation succeeds you'll see the Topstock panel in the corner of the chart, showing the state of all 6 grids, the current hedge level, and the profit target.

A smiley face in the top right of the chart means the EA is active. A cross means Algo Trading still needs enabling.

gated.title: The full guide comes with your purchase
gated.body: This page is an overview so you can see the installation is not complicated. The full guide has screenshots for every step, preset files for NAS100 and US30, an explanation of every parameter, and troubleshooting for the common problems — plus a 30-60 minute setup call with the team.

vps.title: Why you want a VPS
vps.description: MT5 has to stay running whenever the market is open. Running it on a home computer risks the system stopping mid-position.

why.title: Why it matters
why.body: If the computer sleeps, the connection drops, or Windows restarts for an update while a grid is in recovery, the system cannot manage those positions until it is back online.

specs.title: What's enough
specs.body: One MT5 instance running Topstock is not demanding — 2 vCPU and 2 GB of RAM is plenty. Latency to your broker's server matters more than the specification.

providers.title: Rough cost
providers.body: Trading VPS hosting typically runs $5-15 a month. Some brokers provide one free once you hit a volume or deposit threshold, so ask yours first.

cta.title: Didn't find your answer?
cta.description: Ask us directly. We answer every question before you decide to buy.

what.a: It's an Expert Advisor for MetaTrader 5, written in MQL5, built specifically to trade the NASDAQ 100 and US 30 indices. It uses a BUY-only hedge grid strategy with a Fast Points Trail, built on the EMA 20/50/100/200 structure of the AURUM PRO system.

symbols.q: Is it only NAS100, or does US30 work too?
symbols.a: Both. The defaults are tuned for NAS100 volatility. US30 runs on the same values, or slightly tightened — we include a US30 preset with the setup guide.

difference.q: How is it different from other EAs?
difference.a: Most EAs on the market were built for gold or forex and then pointed at indices, where the parameters don't fit. Gold moves 100-300 points a day; NAS100 moves 500-800. Topstock's values were tuned for that scale from the start, and its Fast Points Trail reacts quickly enough for an index.

version.q: What's the latest version, and what changed?
version.a: v1.1, which added the Fast Points Trail: it arms once profit reaches 500 points and trails the stop 300 points behind price, running alongside the original EMA trail and taking whichever is tighter. Existing customers get v1.1 free.

gold.q: Can I use it on XAUUSD (gold)?
gold.a: Technically the parameters are adjustable, but we don't recommend it — everything is tuned for index scale. If you want an EA for gold, AURUM Gold EA is a separate product.

sourceCode.q: Do I get the MQL5 source code?
sourceCode.a: No. You get the compiled .ex5, which is fully functional and lets you adjust every parameter from the input tab, but not the original .mq5 file.

updates.a: No. ฿4,900 covers every update in the v1.x line, for life. We send the new file over LINE whenever one is released.

howToBuy.a: Message us on LINE with your broker and the symbol you're interested in. We run a backtest free and send the report within 24 hours, then talk through the strategy and settings. You only pay if you're happy. There's no pressure.

price.q: What does it cost? Is there a monthly fee?
price.a: ฿4,900 once, for life. No monthly fee, no renewal, no hidden costs.

payment.a: PromptPay for Thai customers (our main option), Thai bank transfer, or Stripe for international customers paying by card. We send payment details once we've talked.

included.q: What do I get for the price?
included.a: The EA v1.1 (.ex5) with presets for NAS100 and US30, unlimited MT5 account activations, free updates across v1.x, a 30-60 minute setup consultation, access to the LINE support group, and a 30-day satisfaction guarantee.

refund.q: Can I get a refund if I'm not satisfied?
refund.a: Yes — a 30-day satisfaction guarantee from the day you receive the files. Contact us on LINE or by email and we'll refund in full through the same method you paid with.

priceCompare.q: How does the price compare to other EAs?
priceCompare.a: Quality EAs run roughly $99-$999, or ฿3,500-฿35,000. At ฿4,900 Topstock sits mid-range — not the cheapest. What differs is the exclusive focus on indices, the free backtest and consultation before buying, and one-to-one support afterwards.

invoice.q: Can you issue a receipt or tax invoice?
invoice.a: Tell us on LINE when you order and we'll prepare the documents with the details you provide.

brokers.a: Any MT5 broker offering NAS100 / US100 / USTEC or US30 / DJ30 that supports hedging accounts. Most of our customers use FBS, Exness, or XM — see the brokers page for details.

minimum.a: $10 on a cent account is enough to test the strategy with real money at very low risk. On a standard account we recommend at least $500 so the grid system has room to work.

centVsStandard.q: What's the difference between a cent and standard account?
centVsStandard.a: A cent account values one lot at a hundredth of a standard account, so you can test with real money at very low risk. We recommend everyone start on cent for at least 2-4 weeks, then move to standard once the behaviour is familiar.

leverage.a: Higher leverage doesn't produce more profit — it gives more margin headroom as a grid grows. 1:200 to 1:500 is generally plenty. What matters more is starting lot size relative to capital, which we work out with you on the setup call.

symbolName.q: My broker's symbol name doesn't match. What now?
symbolName.a: Brokers name it differently — US100, USTEC, NAS100, US100Cash are all the same index. Just drag the EA onto that symbol's chart; it reads the symbol from the chart it's attached to.

multipleAccounts.q: Can I run it on several accounts at once?
multipleAccounts.a: Yes, with no limit on MT5 accounts. You can run a cent account for testing and a live standard account at the same time, or across several brokers.

vps.a: Yes. MT5 has to be running the whole time the market is open, because the EA is managing open grids. We recommend a VPS at around $5-15 a month so the system doesn't stop when your computer sleeps or the connection drops.

timeframe.a: M5 is what we recommend and what the defaults are tuned for. M15 works but produces fewer signals. We don't recommend anything below M5 — the noise overwhelms the entry logic.

settings.q: Do I need to change any settings?
settings.a: The defaults work as-is for NAS100 on a standard account. What you should set for your own capital is the starting lot size and InpRecMaxLevel (the hedge level cap, where we suggest 8-10). We help with both on the setup call.

monitoring.q: Do I need to watch it constantly?
monitoring.a: No, it's fully automated. We do suggest checking in once a day, especially around volatile sessions or major economic releases. The on-chart panel shows all 6 grids at once.

multipleCharts.q: Can I run it on several charts at once?
multipleCharts.a: Yes — NAS100 and US30 together in one account, for instance. Just plan the combined margin carefully, because both charts draw on the same capital to support their grids.

news.q: Should I turn it off around major news?
news.a: That depends on your risk tolerance. Around FOMC or NFP, indices can move violently with high slippage. Some customers disable algo trading through those windows; others leave it running. We can talk it through on the setup call.

drawdown.a: Grid strategies accumulate drawdown when the market trends persistently against the position, because the system adds hedges to average in. The further price runs against you, the deeper it goes. We recommend capping InpRecMaxLevel at 8-10, and never using money you cannot afford to lose entirely.

martingale.a: Not in the doubling sense — lot size does not double each time. Topstock averages in at clearly defined levels, with a cap you set yourself and a close target that scales with position size. That said, every averaging strategy carries the risk of a large loss if the market runs against it far enough for long enough.

worstCase.a: The index falls persistently further than all your hedge levels can absorb, leaving the grid deeply negative and potentially triggering a margin call. That's exactly why we insist on a backtest and a risk conversation before selling, and why we repeat that you should never use money you cannot afford to lose entirely.

capitalAdvice.q: How much should I trade with?
capitalAdvice.a: Only money you accept you could lose in full. Not savings you need to live on, not borrowed money, and not money already committed elsewhere. Always start on a cent account with a small amount.

guarantee.a: No, and we won't. No EA anywhere can guarantee profit, and past performance says nothing about the future. Topstock is a software tool, not investment advice, and AURUM TECH is not a licensed financial advisor.

channels.a: LINE is the main channel and the fastest. There's also Telegram for international customers, and email for anything you want in writing.

hours.a: Monday to Friday, 9:00-18:00 Thailand time. Message outside those hours too and we'll reply on the next working day.

language.a: Thai and English — for pre-sale questions, the setup call, and support afterwards.

activationHelp.q: What if I have trouble installing it?
activationHelp.a: We'll help. Every customer gets a 30-60 minute setup call and access to the LINE support group. If installation, configuration, or behaviour isn't right, just message us.
